html:
The Montagnais are the southern Innu, an Algonquian people of the north shore of the St Lawrence River in Quebec and of Labrador. "Montagnais" is French for "mountain people".

They hunted moose and caribou, fished, and moved by canoe in summer and snowshoe in winter. The Naskapi to the north are close relatives.

In 1603 Innu leaders at Tadoussac made an alliance with Samuel de Champlain, and they became key partners of New France in the fur trade, against their enemies the Haudenosaunee. Quebec City was founded on their land in 1608. The Jesuit Paul Le Jeune spent a winter with an Innu band in 1633 and 1634, and his account in the Jesuit Relations is one of the fullest early pictures of their life. Today most Innu live in communities in Quebec and Labrador.
